text:
anya: Heads-up—QA caught ambiguous client behavior when a route falls back to cheaper models. Sometimes we return 503, sometimes 429, and clients keep retrying blindly. Can we agree a single, machine-friendly surface for routing/quota/degrade signals?

david: +1. We need separation between (a) rate/quota exhaustion and (b) graceful degradation/fallback. 429 for client-rate/quota; 503 for service degradation makes sense, but we should attach a clear subcode header so SDKs can map to retry vs fallback.

lina: Suggestion: compact headers over body fields. Bodies are inconsistent across SDKs. Proposal: `X-RW-Error-Type` and `X-RW-Error-Subcode` with standardized values. Example: `X-RW-Error-Type: client_quota` / `X-RW-Error-Subcode: quota_per_minute`.

maria: +1 to headers. Also we should keep an explicit `Retry-After` for 429 only. For 503 we could include `X-RW-Failmode: degraded` to indicate fallback happened and whether the output may be lower-quality.

anya: I'm worried about backwards compatibility. We already return `error.code` in body for older clients. Any migration plan must avoid breaking SDKs that currently parse body.

david: Migration plan: emit both for a transition period. Headers are primary, body `error.code` mirrors header. We'll document and add SDK helpers to prefer header when present.

patrick: We also need telemetry signals. For routing policies we want `route_policy` and `route_variant` in traces and metrics. Otherwise we won't be able to tell if errors are caused by policy routing, capacity, or customer quota.

lina: Agreed. Telemetry fields proposal: `routing_policy`, `model_variant`, `client_visible` boolean. `client_visible=true` when we intentionally surface an actionable hint to the caller (e.g., quota or retryable).

maria: UX: Console badges should map to these signals. For example: orange badge "degraded (fallback)" when `X-RW-Failmode: degraded` is seen, red "quota" when 429 rate. But we need to avoid double-counting—choose primary signal precedence: quota > capacity > degraded.

anya: One open question: HTTP 424 vs 409 for precondition-like rejections (e.g. tenant budget exceeded). Any thoughts?

david: 409 is confusing. 424 (Failed Dependency) feels off too. I prefer 402-ish semantics (payment/billing) but we shouldn't invent new status. We could keep 429 but include `X-RW-Error-Subcode: tenant_budget_exceeded` and treat it as non-retryable in SDKs.

lina: That works. SDKs should treat certain subcodes as terminal (no retry) and others as retryable with backoff. We need a server-side canonical list and a small sample mapping in the repo.

maria: Also propose we add a per-route telemetry counter `client_error_class` with values: quota, rate, terminal_billing, degraded, transient_capacity, internal_error. That will help console rollups and runbooks.

anya: Good. For rollout safety: we'll enable headers in canary 10% first. SDKs will be updated to read headers but fall back to body if absent. We'll add a flag in console to mark routes opted into header schema.

patrick: Ops note: add log lines when we set `X-RW-Failmode` so SRE can trace from logs->traces->console. Also add metric tag `exposure: header` vs `exposure: body` for rollout monitoring.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canaries scheduled: eng-platform/canary/615555 -> 2026-03-22T02:00Z (10%).

anya: Action items: (1) eng-platform: RFC doc with canonical header + subcode list + retry semantics (lina) (2) SDKs: read headers, fallback to body; publish patch (david) (3) Console: badge mapping + precedence rules + telemetry fields (maria) (4) SRE: instrumentation hooks for `X-RW-Failmode` logs and metric tag (patrick). I'll draft the RFC in the docs repo and ping y'all.

david: Thanks — I'll start the SDK PR and add unit tests for terminal vs retryable subcodes.

lina: I'll put a draft of the header/enums in the RFC and include example responses: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RW-Error-Type: client_quota
X-RW-Error-Subcode: quota_per_minute
Retry-After: 60
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": { "code": "QUOTA_PER_MINUTE", "message": "Rate limit exceeded" } }
```

anya: Perfect. Keep messages short in the RFC — console teams just want the mapping table. Closing thread here, will link RFC shortly. :thumbsup:
